utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the record I must lodge an objection to the length of the cross-examination as compared to the length of the direct examination. I think Madam Registrar will inform you that Mr. Krsnik had this witness on approximately 30 minutes. I believe that's correct. 45 at the most. In any event, Your Honours, we object to allowing the Prosecutor two to three to four times the amount of cross-examination than we took on direct examination. I want to make that contemporaneous and I want to make it continuing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, I believe that you're prejudging the result of the cross-examination. I think Mr. Scott only spent a few minutes before we broke. We will see how long the Prosecution will last. Yes, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I can provide the accurate calculations during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. And Mr. Scott, it is our intention to give more time to Martinovic's Defence for their preparation next week. We hope we could wind up all the witnesses for Mr. Naletilic this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. President, Your Honours, based on the schedule I saw from the Naletilic Defence at the end of last week I have no reason to believe that we can't finish the so-called live witnesses this week relatively -- relatively easily. That is I don't think pressing too much at the end of the week. As the Chamber knows, there remains a significant number of witnesses for videolink and frankly, it may be a larger number than any of us had fully anticipated, when one looks at the most current list and including one that had been approved for videolink before, I think the list now looks something around nine additional witnesses. I just point that out for the Chamber's consideration. We may not be as close to completing the Naletilic case. Let me be very clear, I'm distinguishing between the live witnesses this week, which I don't anticipate any problems finishing, but beyond this week I think the Chamber may find, depending on which witness actually appear at the end of the day, that there are actually substantially more Tuta Defence left than you may have anticipated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much about reminding us about this situation. And Mr. Krsnik, we are not debating at this moment. We have been informed that those videolink witnesses are very short witnesses. Originally they were arranged for the deposition in Mostar but unfortunately, we cancelled that arrangement. So we'll do our best to accommodate the request from the Defence counsel. Now, could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: While we are preparing I'll just indicate to Madam Registrar, that we will continue on with the bundle of document that is we distributed on Friday. And the next two exhibits, just to help us move along efficiently would be 250.1 and 503.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, since there are so many documents in this bundle, would you please give us more documents you are going to use in the list so that the Registrar could be very prepared beforehand?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Your Honour, counting -- if time allows I hope to get through most of these exhibits but it's certainly possible, it's more than possible, that given time constraints we may not get through them all. I can tell the Registrar that in addition to the ones I've just mentioned, 250.1, 503.1, 524.3, 268.1, and 702.1 would be the first, however many that is, five or six exhibits that I hope to move rather quickly through so if we could pull those out. We would be -- thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest during the weekend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. We will start. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Scott: [continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness NR.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to start, please, by asking you since you began your testimony on Friday or on Friday, excuse me, have you talked with anyone and I specifically use the word anyone, any person at all, about your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't talked to anybody about my testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I just want to be very clear with you that my question is all-encompassing. I do not want to pry into private family matters but for example you didn't talk to even a family member on the telephone or anything about your testimony or appearance here in The Hague; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't talked with anybody about the subject of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm going to ask you what may sound like a very similar question, but it's a bit different, so please listen to my question. Has anyone talked to you whether you said any words or responded or not, has anyone talked to you about your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not about the testimony, but my friends who are in the hotel have talked to me but we haven't talked about this particular subject.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And the final question on this point, sir, have you reviewed -- since you began testifying, has anyone, I again I use the word anyone, shown you any documents that you should -- that someone thought perhaps you should see or study before your testimony? Have you looked at any document since you began testifying on Friday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody has showed me anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, sir. Now, would it be correct, sir, just to try to finish up on the beginnings of the Baja Kraljevic ATG --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps we should go to private session for a question that might tend to identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown we will not put these on the ELMO for protective measures purposes but can the witness please now be handed -- it will help us go as quickly as possible if he could please be handed 250.1, 503.1, 524.3? Let's start with those three, please. Sir, I'd like you to first just look briefly, I'm not going to ask you extensive questions about these initial documents, but let me just ask briefly at 250.1, does this appear to be a certificate dated the 15th of -- excuse me, 16th of February, 1993 indicating that a Lasic was a member of the Baja Kraljevic ATG from approximately 20 May, 1992, until what I assume what this means is to the current time?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I am told that the transcript has stopped. Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, that Mr. Lasic was a member of my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is that your signature on the Croatian language original or copy of the original? Is that your signature -- excuse me, strike that. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No this is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that -- sorry? Is it correct, however, sir, that at least during the time from the May of 1992, until -- and while this document was in effect, this -- I'm trying to decide, Your Honour, if we have to be in private session or not. I suppose out of an abundance of caution we should be in private session, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go back to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could ask the witness please be shown Exhibit P17.3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While that's being handed to you, sir, do you recall knowing an HVO officer by the name of Zeljko Bosnjak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Mr. Bosnjak's photo. I did know the gentleman. We participated in the operation to liberate Mostar in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps that could be -- I think everyone has it but perhaps that can be put on the ELMO. It may assist. And did you know Mr. Bosnjak to hold any position of command or -- he was an officer or commander in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. one -- well, let me start over again. Was he an officer in the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was in the Convicts Battalion, Mr. Bosnjak did not hold any command positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was up until mid-1992. But after you left the Convicts Battalion, as you've told us, at any time after that, so far as you know, did Mr. Bosnjak hold any position as an officer or commander of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I know that Mr. Bosnjak was killed in 1993 in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you telling the Chamber that apart from operating with him in the liberation of Mostar in approximately May or June, 1992, that you had no other dealings with this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We would come across each other. I knew him. But that was all -- that was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What unit -- if you can assist us, if you know or can give us an idea, what unit do you associate him with, Mr. Bosnjak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I first met him, that was in -- during the liberation of Mostar, Mr. Bosnjak was a member of the mortar unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the Convicts Battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, not of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, well which unit I'm not talking about a mortar unit, the name of which unit, which company, brigade, battalion, what HVO formation did you associate Mr. Bosnjak with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Poskok Battalion from Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir, I only have time for a couple of questions on the next topic. Were you ever familiar with another ATG called the Benko Penavic ATG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question? Did you say Vinko Penavic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My apology, if I said it incorrectly. Benko Penavic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about the Benko Penavic ATG which was operating in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know who formed that ATG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the headquarters, the Main Staff, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the record is clear, you're referring to the HVO Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Main Staff which was authorised to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the -- was there a man named Mario Milicevic the commander officer of that ATG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew Mr. Milicevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was called Baja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he the commanding officer of that unit throughout its existence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commanding officer, but whether he was the commanding officer throughout the existence of this unit, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the ATG Benko Penavic and the ATG Baja Kraljevic, ever operate together during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They never operated together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell me, sir, have you had any dealings or contact of any sort, whether professional, personal or social, with Mr. Milicevic, say in 2001 or 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you say during 2001 and 2002?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never saw this gentleman during those two years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was waiting until we came to the years 2001 and 2002. Of course, I do not know how the learned friend will continue in his cross-examination, but I certainly would like to object for questions to be put to this witness in relation to the years 2002 and 2001. I think we have been really spending too much time and I went through some of the other exhibits and it seems to me that they are to a large extent also those that have to do with the year 2001, 2002. They have to do with the OHR, and I think that we are really only wasting our precious time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this moment, we don't know where this -- where Mr. Prosecutor is going to lead us, but I believe this question has somehow related to the credibility of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And maybe Mr. Scott could shed some light on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If time allows, only if time allows it will be connected up to some later parts of my question and I don't intend to pursue it further at this moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you assist the Chamber with this? Is the term "cabinet" have any meaning to you in connection with an HVO political official or military officer having a quote "cabinet," however that phrase is interpreted to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't answer your question as to what means. Maybe it's an office or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this, then. Maybe it will assist to make it a bit more concrete. If documents, for instance, were to indicate that an officer or an official had a cabinet, of simply, by example seven persons, a cabinet of seven persons, what would that mean to you, based on your experience in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally never had a cabinet. I had an office. I had a secretary. And I really couldn't answer this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever know documents indicating that Mr. Naletilic had a cabinet of five persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I haven't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after you left -- sorry, Mr. President, I'm just checking what session. We are in open session, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps we should go to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, this appears to be a document related to a record related to the 22nd sabotage detachment. I simply show it to you to ask you this question: Was a man named Ivo Rozic ever a commander, part -- excuse me a commander of the 22nd sabotage detachment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was one of the lower ranking commanders in this unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is it correct, sir, that as many of these units moved from the Convicts Battalion or the ATGs into other units at the end of 1993, or 199-- beginning of 1994, that Vinko Martinovic, Stela, also became a member of the 22nd Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall it, Mr. Martinovic was not a member of the 22nd Sabotage Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown Exhibits 818 and 819? 818 and 819, and sir, I'm going to direct your attention to them in reverse order, if I can ask you please to look at 819 first? I'll just caution you, sir, if any of these documents have your name on them please don't mention your name unless I specifically ask you a question about it in which case I'll move to private session. If you look first of all to 819, this would appear to indicate a number of individuals, including Vinko Martinovic, Dubravko Pehar and Ernest Takac. Moving for a very short time to something called the ATJ, anti-terrorist group "Domovina.". Do you recall anything about the ATJ Domovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that ATJ Domovina existed, but whether these men were members of this unit, I wouldn't know really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 819, do you recognise the signatures, if you do, or the name on the Croatian language original, Ivan Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see it under my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see we are at the break time but if you would allow me two or three questions I'll try to finish it before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you'll direct your attention to 818, this appears to be a very similar certificate, concerning the same five individuals, indicating that they were members of the 22nd sabotage detachment. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do. I see that this is written here but why the document was issued, why the gentleman signed it, I really wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you assist the Chamber -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that this document was issued on the 10th of October, 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir, no question about that. If you look at Exhibit -- go back to Exhibit 819 for a moment, for all these individuals -- well they are not exactly same but let's focus on Mr. Martinovic. This document which also purports to be signed by Mr. Martinovic in the far -- next to the last right column, would indicate that he was a member of the ATJ Domovina between June and October, 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know. I was not the commander at that time. I really couldn't confirm to you whether this is correct or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness answered and let me immediately emphasise that the cross-examination should be conducted in a fair way, because these are identical documents and they bear the identical dates. One referring to ATJ Domovina and the other referring to the 22nd Sabotage Detachment. The same date of the same year, somebody issued a document confirming that these same persons were members of two different units. Could you please compare these two documents and the dates?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, no dispute about it. The documents are clear on their face and I've never suggested anything to the contrary to what Mr. Krsnik just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, why doesn't, then, the learned friend ask the witness for what purpose this list, this document, was issued? Then everybody will be in quite clear minds as to what was the purpose. If the learned friend doesn't ask the question, I will have to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to state, Your Honours, that this question alluded to the fact that Vinko Martinovic had signed this document. Obviously this is not the way to establish this fact. This should be done in a different manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, I think there is some -- something unclear concerning the two documents. Would you please ask a few more questions to this witness so that to clarify the certain issues for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I'll try to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, there is no dispute, never was, that both these documents appear to be dated the 10th of October, 1996, listing members, in particular HVO units. 819 appears to be under -- over the name of Ivan Andabak whereas 818 covering the same soldiers but for a different time period, appears to be prepared over -- I'm not suggesting it's your signature yet, but over your name as commander of that unit. Now do you see all that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I see that my name is handwritten, not typed, but this is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, were you the -- check to see what's -- we are in public. Mr. President, I'm sorry but I suppose we should go to private session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, before we leave the subject, I think once and for all of the 22nd Sabotage Detachment or unit, is it true, sir, that that unit was named after a famous elite unit in World War II?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is first time I hear it, from you, that the unit was named after some other unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have no information, sir, and you've never heard, that it was named after the 22nd Ustasha Battalion established in 1944?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge whatsoever about that. I really I hear this for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask the witness please be shown Exhibit 798.1?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you can look at the Croatian language version of 798.01, I asked you earlier this morning about a cabinet. Do you recall having any information around -- that around July of 1995, and for whatever reason the translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, the translation of the document has left a question mark in the date column, but respectfully, I would suggest that if you look at the attached, both the typed version and the handwritten version of the Croatian language originals, it seems to be Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. rather apparent that it's 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, Mr. Naletilic having a cabinet of five persons at any time during your association with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that Naletilic had a cabinet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document appears to be, and again I'm not saying it's your signature and it would appear the contrary, but this order or document was prepared over your name, I'm not going to mention your name, as commander. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that, but this is not my signature. And I don't know why this would be sent to a cabinet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, that's why I'm asking you. This is a document prepared over your position as commander, and purportedly over your name, information is being reported that Mr. Naletilic had a quote cabinet of five individuals. Now, can you assist the Chamber with any more information about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information at all. I see this document for the first time, and as you have said it yourself, this is not my signature. Anybody could have typed this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, obviously we are going to put forth all of our objections to documents later on, but where did the Prosecutor get the information that the cabinet consisted of five people? This is simply a minus, minus 105, minus 7. If you -- [In English] Also in English version it's also minus. [Interpretation] And I really don't know whence the allegation on the part of my learned friend that this is a cabinet consisting of five people, whereas this is simply minus five. And this is the year 1995, and this is an order issued by somebody called Livno OG [phoen].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: If you look at all the totals there is no minus sign in front of it, so it's obviously a style of typing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But of what? There is also mention of Risovac base, the things that have been written off, but what has been written off? To my mind, this is a minus. When we are talking about things being written off. The second group is things being written off. I don't know how it is -- it has been translated into English, outgoings are things written off. I don't know. When it says "cabinet," the Prosecutor claims it refers to people. I really don't know where -- whence the allegation comes from.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the Prosecutor is just asking a question about this document and from this document, it's clear cabinet of General Naletilic is there. So I think the Prosecutor is entitled to ask a question concerning with this document. And I also believe that the witness has the full right to confirm or deny any questions put forward by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: For the record, then, Your Honour, we would object to relevancy. This is one and a half years after the scope of the indictment in which Mr. Naletilic is being tried in this war crimes trial. And this is way outside the scope of the indictment. There is no relevance to this. And we wasted 30 minutes on this type of questioning. And for the record, Your Honour, Mr. Krsnik spent 30 minutes on direct examination and Mr. Scott now has tripled that and he's still going. It's to Your Honours to cut him off whenever you want to, or if you don't want to that's fine but we believe the equality of arms is being shattered in this case and we wants our record noted for -- our objection noted for the record, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you, Mr. Meek for reminding us about time limits. At the beginning of this -- to this sitting we already told Mr. Scott about the time limit and he promised us that on the whole, he could finish all the witnesses this week. Maybe for one witness, it will take more time or maybe for the other witnesses, the time used by the Prosecution will be shorter, and I believe that Mr. Scott is trying to wind up his cross-examination as soon as possible. Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, at the risk of using some of my precious time let me respond by agreeing with what you've just said, Mr. President. I have no question -- well, I have no reason to believe that there is going to be any trouble completing these witnesses this week. In fact probably by mid-week. I anticipate no problem with that. However, this witness, as far as I can tell, I would have to go back and look at the Defence witness again, will be the only senior deputy of the accused Naletilic that will be called in this trial. He is uniquely situated. And it very well may be that as opposed to other witnesses, including some of the other witnesses yet to appear this week, that it may be that there will be fuller cross-examination of this witness and less cross-examination of other witnesses but in any event, I see absolutely no reason to think we will not conclude these witnesses by Wednesday. So I would appreciate -- I appreciate, Mr. President, your patience and I'm trying I think the Court will know from my questions because frankly there are a number of these topics that I could have pursued more extensively and I'm doing it in a very appreciated fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But Your Honours, this calls for reply. How come my learned friend can say that this is the only high-ranking deputy commander? We have had people here who were high ranking officers than this witness here, from the chief of the general staff to all the others. They all had a higher rank, they were all higher ranking commanders than this gentleman here. I don't know what the Prosecution is saying. We had objected on a number of occasions about the length of cross-examination. The Prosecution has spent over an hour on irrelevant documents, referring to the period one year after the indicted -- indictment. There were witnesses in the courtroom. We have their CVs, we know who they are and some of them were so much higher ranking officers than this gentleman here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I believe that the different judgement of the witness, maybe on your side you believe some witnesses are more important than this one, but as clearly stated by the Prosecution -- by Mr. Prosecutor, that he believes that this witness is important one. But any way, we have to move. Yes, Mr. Scott. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I must note it's now approximately five minutes after 11 and I've hardly had a question since starting from the break but I am trying to move forward. Mr. President, in light of those constraints I'm not going to it argue about Exhibit 798.01 any more. I suggest, I do not want to interpret the document. I don't think it's appropriate for Mr. Krsnik to try to interpret the document. To the extent he's done so these are what might be referred to it as bullet items simply indicating numbers and the -- the math as the Chamber already indicates these items are being added together and the math seems to be correct. Because of time, I'll have to leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it correct and you would agree with me, wouldn't you, that Mr. Naletilic was a commander in 1992, he was a combat commander, leading Bosnian Croat armed forces in 1992, including the liberation of Mostar? You and I can agree on that; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Naletilic was the commander of the Convicts Battalion unit until the end of August, as far as I know. After -- and I don't know that he was the commander of the overall operations. I know that he was the commander of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't it also correct, sir, that Mr. Naletilic was again a commander in 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he wasn't. I don't know what unit are you referring to. I know that he was the deputy mayor of Siroki Brijeg at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember an operation named -- and I may get this wrong so forgive me, Cincar? C-I-N-C-A-R

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: When was that operation taking place?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately November, 1994.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, sir, that in early in that operation, or that campaign, your unit at that time was on the left flank along with a unit being under the command of Ivan Andabak? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that my unit participated in that operation. Whether I was on the left flank, I can't remember. Mr. Andabak at the time was the commander of all special units so it is possible that he was in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it correct that Mr. Naletilic, at least for a time, was the overall commander of that operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'd like the witness to please be shown Exhibit 787.2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'll ask to you cast your eyes on that document for a moment please, 787.2 in the Croatian language version, while you're doing so, let me state to you for the record this appears to be a report from Miroslav Tudjman, the son of President Franjo Tudjman, who at that time was the direct of the Croatian Intelligence Service, HIS, reporting to his father, the President of Croatia. If I can direct your particular attention, please, to the -- approximately the middle of the first -- little below the -- halfway down the first page in your Croatian language and for the Courtroom the bottom of the first page of the report, second page of the exhibit. Is it not stated, sir, "It has been noticed that the commander, chief of the general staff of the HVO, General Tihomir Blaskic has off everyone being absent from the headquarters of the Cincar operation. Presents at the headquarters are Mladen Naletilic, aka Tuta, who was trying to direct the operation, General Praljak, Vice Vukojevic and Ciro Grubisic also visited the headquarters at Sujica. Now, isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that the headquarters were in Sujica. I came for briefings during the operation and I never saw Mr. Naletilic up there. I saw the commander, Tihomir Blaskic and when he wasn't there, there was General Praljak. I don't know why would Mr. Naletilic command this operation? He didn't even have a rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May we lodge a continuing objection contemporaneously with all of these documents that are way outside the scope of this indictment, so we don't have to keep getting on our feet when we talk about 1994, 1995, 1996?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Your objection is registered in the transcript already. And I believe those questions are related to the credibility of this witness because this witness participated in certain actions at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if I could have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm looking at the source of this document, in the description, this is a new document, and it says Zagreb Archives. Your Honours, please look at the Croatian original. There is no stamp of the Zagreb Archives anywhere on the document. We already know that every page should bear the stamp of the Zagreb Archives. We have established that. And this stamp is missing from the Croatian original of this exhibit. There is no stamp on any of its pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much to draw our attention to that problem of this document. But I really believe that you have to raise this issue at a later stage, when we are admitting the documents. You may proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think we should go to private session for a question or two that would identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that during the war and in fact since the war, Mr. Naletilic, Tuta, has been regarded by very many people in the Siroki Brijeg area, perhaps even the broader Mostar region, as a war hero?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Naletilic has been considered a war hero, because he takes a lot of credit for the liberation of Siroki Brijeg and Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that for a very long time, there were many posters and graffiti painted on walls around Siroki Brijeg saying for example, words to the effect, "We love Tuta"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Even to this very day, you can see it in Siroki Brijeg. It does say, a number of places, that people love Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask the witness be shown -- Mr. President, I have not had a chance to make a copy of this. I ask that it be referred to in the record as Exhibit 939 but if the usher could assist me in showing this to the witness please and perhaps it can be held up so that everyone in the courtroom can see it. Show that first to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen a poster like that before, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The whole of Siroki Brijeg, the whole of Herzegovina, were full of this sort of posters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, can I have your assist assistance to show that so that the Judges and the other people in the courtroom can see it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, perhaps you can assist us by interpreting, what are the two words on the bottom of that poster indicate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, "Our victory".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say these posters were not only in Siroki Brijeg but throughout Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. People, wherever they loved Naletilic, they would put up a poster like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that perhaps for you personally and for many people, coming to The Hague to testify from the Siroki Brijeg or Mostar region, they are to come here and say something which might be interpreted to reflect negatively or to some how implicate Mr. Naletilic in crime, that for their -- in their view and perhaps in your view, you would be doing damage to a war hero?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since this was a very lengthy question, could, please, the Prosecutor make it more concise and shorter?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me try to make it more specific and maybe it will be more concrete in that way. I'm only saying this as an example, sir, so please understand that. If, for example, you were to testify make it very clear that throughout 1993, Mr. Naletilic was in fact the commander of the Convicts Battalion and commander of the ATG Baja Kraljevic, you would know, wouldn't you, that that would be very detrimental to Mr. Naletilic in the case here? Wouldn't you? I'll ask the second part of my question after that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I say that Mr. Naletilic was a commander in 1993 when this is not true?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But sir, if you gave that testimony, isn't it true that you and others -- I'm trying to rephrase the question in the way you asked me -- would essentially be giving damning testimony against someone that you regard as a war hero?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I here solemnly declared that I will speak the truth, and this is what I am doing. Through this solemn declaration, you have put the responsibility and obligation on me to tell the truth and only the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, just in fairness to the Chamber, I would indicate that I am shortening and trying to finish my exam. I have five remaining documents and the rest I will forgo, but I would like the witness to see five remaining documents on these issues if the usher could please show the witness 208.1? I'm sorry, I think the translations -- my apology. These are loose. Some of these documents had not been translate Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. as of Friday. That's why they are in separate bundles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document dated the 5th of January, 1993. Does it not indicate that a man named -- I believe it's at least in part a French name, but perhaps Michel Tandrovic [phoen], was a member of the ATG Baja Kraljevic "under command of Mr. Tuta who is currently residing in Mostar"? Isn't that what the document says, sir, and isn't it true that Mr. Naletilic was the commander of the Baja Kraljevic ATG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct. I was the commander of the ATG Baja Kraljevic, not Mr. Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't think the military police of the HVO knew who the commander of the Baja Kraljevic ATG was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe the person who was drafting this document didn't know it but the HVO police did know very well who the ATG Baja Kraljevic commander had been.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I ask the usher's assistance with Exhibit 270.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, as a procedural matter and as an objection I believe the Prosecutor is now violating this Trial Chamber's order that all documents to be shown to the witnesses on cross-examination must be provided to counsel for the other party prior to the cross-examination and not during the cross-examination, which is happening right now and we object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as we ruled the other day, that nobody could predict what will happen during the cross-examination. In this case, a few documents could be furnished during the cross-examination. You may proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This appears to be a report by or a request, excuse me, dated the 1st of April, 1993, again -- please I'm saying very specifically over the name of Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, as commander, to Mr. Bruno Stojic, the Minister of Defence, concerning fuel coupons for the Convicts Battalion and the Baja Kraljevic ATG. My question to you is this: Isn't it true that Mr. Naletilic effectively commanded, if they were separate at all, both units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Naletilic was not the commander of both units. I personally was the commander of ATG Baja Kraljevic and Mr. Andabak and Mr. Hrkac at that time were the commanders of the Convicts Battalion at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I ask the witness to be shown Exhibit 428, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have nothing against this. The discussion is a lively sort of process. Justice should be done and, of course this, is what you are trying to achieve, but wouldn't it be a larger question to put what is the source of these documents? In earlier documents it was very clearly stated what the source was. We here have entire, fully new documents. We have nothing, no knowledge about the source of these documents. They were not tendered in earlier on, and they are just now being pulled out of the sleeve for the cross-examination. So what are the sources? What are these documents? Are we going really to insist in the translated document that the document in original was signed? Because it says, "Signature Mladen Naletilic." In the original there are no signatures. Certainly we would well committee any information whatsoever about the source of these documents. And Your Honours, I'd like to conclude for the record, I do not believe that these documents were translated on Friday. That's all I wanted to say. For the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I saw a stamp on the right top corner of the Croatian documents. Maybe Mr. Scott could tell us in a few words.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I'll be happy to do all that. I don't know that it's necessary in to do it in the time allocated to examine the witness, but I will do so. In using Exhibit 270.1, in the upper right corner of the Croatian language original, you will see, for example, the archive stamp. Admittedly not particularly legible but having seen hundreds, if not thousands of those, Mr. President, I think I can represent to you in answering counsel's question that that's the source. Some of the documents, Mr. President, have been translated before, some were not. As you just indicated Mr. President, a few additional, handful of approximately four or five documents were identified since Friday afternoon and I put them to this witness and I believe it's fair to do so. I also finally would comment, Your Honour, this has happened throughout the time in which Mr. Krsnik has accused various members of the Prosecution team of bad faith in connection with the signature on the document, and it's happened again just now. No one suggested, I think the transcript will show, no one suggested for a moment that Mr. Naletilic had signed this. Nor does the translation. If you look at the English translation, Mr. President, Your Honours, it simply says signed. Signed by someone. There is no indication on the translation, page 2, there is no indication that it was signed by Tuta. Just says signed. And the Croatian language original will show that indeed the document was signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you want to hear my view, I will tell you what I believe. I certainly do not believe that the Prosecution is acting in a bona fide sense but you cannot ask the translators to say, "Signed by Tuta," when it says very clearly in the original Ivan Andabak. If it says Andabak or you can't read the signature, you cannot put in the translation, "Signed by Mr. Naletilic." And this is one of the many reasons that I do not trust that you are a bona fide Prosecution office. I apologise, Mr. President, but I'd like to say very clearly that the Defence counsel or I myself personally Kresimir Krsnik, do not believe in the bona fide approach by the prosecutors. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, we would like to thank you very much to draw our attention to the translation of this document, but I don't think it's the time for both parties to debate on the bona fide matters. We have to finish the testimony of this witness as soon as possible. Let us move on. Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 428? I think it was the one -- I think we were in the process of doing so before these last interventions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document dated the 2nd of June, 1993. Does it not over the typed name of Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, as commander of the Convicts Battalion, request money for weapons for rifles for both the Convicts Battalion and the ATG Baja Kraljevic in June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says here that money is requested for the Convicts Battalion and for the Baja Kraljevic ATG. However, I do not understand why Mr. Andabak requested that money be made available for my unit. If anybody were to request the funds, I, as a commander, should have done it, and it is the first time that I see this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you this: You were an HVO commander, relatively senior commander. Not at the most senior level, but a relatively senior unit commander involved in these matters. I will tell you, I think it's fair, Mr. President will correct me if I'm wrong but it's fair to say that the Judges have seen a number of documents signed by Mr. -- purporting to be signed by Mr. Andabak in that fashion. Did you ever know anyone in the HVO, Mr. Bruno Stojic or anyone, the issue ever to be raised to this effect, sir, you continue to send us documents signed by the wrong person, we will not authorise action, we will not give you money for rifles, we will not give you flats we will not give you logistical support because the wrong person is signing these orders? To your knowledge, did that ever happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would request the Prosecutor to put me one direct question and not 15 questions all at a time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of any request from -- coming from the Convicts Battalion or the Baja Kraljevic ATG in your experience, in 1993, that was rejected by the HVO command because it was signed by the wrong person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of why somebody would request money for two units because after all, each unit had its own commander. And I'm not aware of any such document. Whatever I requested for my own unit, I would always sign such a request myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Exhibit 649.1, please, which I believe has already been admitted. I would note, Mr. President, some of these documents have already been admitted which is another reason why -- I have it here, sir. If the witness could please be shown 649.1? I'm is I've simply made additional copies to assist the courtroom, Mr. President, so people don't have to go to their binders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, this document indicates in a report signed by -- or coming over the name Stanko Bozic, dated the 16th of October, 1993, that a member of the Baja Kraljevic ATG, a Mr. Reuf Ajanovic, took a prisoner from the Heliodrom to Siroki Brijeg on the order of Mladen Naletilic, Tuta. Now, you know that to be true, and more generally you knew that, in fact, Tuta had the ability to issue orders to do such things, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that on the 13th of October, 1993, upon an oral order by Mr. Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, Reuf Ajanovic, a MP, military policeman, as being a member of the ATG, but members of Baja Kraljevic -- he was never a member of Baja Kraljevic, and Baja Kraljevic ATG members never had any insignia of -- or any badges of the military police. But he obviously, as the document says, produced a badge of a member of the military police. Furthermore, this had all been going on at the time when I was on sick leave. Therefore, I really do not know what was going on at that time. I can only tell you that Mr. Ajanovic never was a member of Baja Kraljevic ATG.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the Baja Kraljevic ATG was based at the Heliodrom, was it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I come back to the question I raised with you earlier. Isn't it true, sir, that on a number of occasions, that that unit and such close proximity to the Muslim prisoners at the Heliodrom, took or released Muslim prisoners on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct, that we would either take or release prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And Mr. President, as I indicated either my last or next to last document, Exhibit 733.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could the Prosecutor tell me whether this document could not be translated before Friday again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Which document do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The one we've just received. 733. P733. Is the learned friend implying that this was not translated by Friday?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, I'm not, I'm not, Mr. President, and I'm not going to engage -- unless the Court tells me too I'm not going to engage in colloquy with counsel. I can tell the Chamber that as I sat in my office on Friday afternoon reviewing documents. There were a number of documents that as of Friday I did not have translations of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krsnik, you were requested many times before to raise these formal issues at a later point in time, when the witness is not in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, directing your attention to Exhibit 733, dated the 29th of December, 1993. This is an order from General Ante Roso, chief of the HVO Main Staff, appears to be indicated directed to General Mladen Naletilic, aka Tuta, personally. It's a -- has at least six numbered paragraphs with paragraph 5 beak broken down into subparagraphs. It's an order directly to Mr. Naletilic, sir, and in five -- directing your particular attention to 5.1, does not General Roso, at that time, issue the order the Tuta ATG dash the Convicts Battalion, Baja Kraljevic and Benko Penavic battalions and others under your command, besides the engagement of the forces so far, shall form a reserve of main forces as follows"? And then it continues. Isn't that what it says, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says in this document, under 5.1, ATG Tuta/Convicts Battalion, Baja Kraljevic Battalion and Benko Penavic, yes, but I do not see anywhere in this -- under this item the name of Mladen Naletilic, Tuta. And the order was issued on the 29th of December, 1993, when Mr. Sopta and myself, Mr. Sopta was the commander of the 2nd Guards Brigade --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't identify yourself because we are in open session. I just caution you. You can continue.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two of us were preparing the structure for the 2nd Guards Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Brigade. I was absent at the time and I really was not familiar with all these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir, allowing for the fact -- and no dispute that there this was a time of translation, late 1993, early 1994, the Chamber has heard about the 2nd Guards Brigade and the Chamber has heard about the 22nd Sabotage Detachment. But is this not an order from the general, the Chief of the Main Staff, Ante Roso, directed to Mr. Naletilic as commander of the Convicts Battalion, Baja Kraljevic and Benko Penavic units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the last page, it says, "To be submitted to the Mostar area, to the -- Tuta ATG, and to the archives." Who they were referring to as ATG Tuta, I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my final question to you is this: Didn't you also know at that time that General Roso had just recently come to Bosnia and Herzegovina as a -- from being a very senior officer in the Croatian Army and been appointed to that position in fact by President Franjo Tudjman of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know who appointed General Roso. I know that he came, who he had been appointed by, I really am not familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll ask that the witness please be shown 6 -- my last Exhibit Mr. President, 664.2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Directing your attention, sir, to the Croatian language original document to orient yourself. This appears to be a document dated the 6th of November, 1993, over the names, again to avoid dispute, I specifically say over the names, of General Janko Bobetko, chief of the HV Croatian Army Main Staff and the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Croatia, Gojko Susak, and by this document, sir, doesn't this indicate that 14 senior members of the Croatian Army were appointed around the early November, 1993, to the most senior positions of the HVO, including General Roso?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, it's the first time that I see this document, and I see that this document is neither signed nor authorised. Therefore I really can say nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me be very clear to you. My questions are not limited to what's on this document or your knowledge. But as I said to you a few moments ago you were a senior HVO officer during this time and you knew this department from -- whether you ever saw this document or not, you know the contents of it to be true, don't you, all these senior officers include General Ante Roso; Miljenko Crnjek; Marjan Biskic; number 9, Ivan Bagaric; Brigadier of medical profession, Dr. Ivan Bagaric, as chief of the medical corps; you knew all this information, you know today, don't you, that this information is true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know that. I met Mr. Roso. All the other officers that you -- whose names you mentioned, I do not know. And I'm not familiar with this document. I wasn't that high-ranking officer who familiarised with who will be sent from Zagreb to our area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall in late 1993 a number of new units appearing in Herzegovina? And I direct your attention specifically to item roman numeral 2 where it says "all units under the command of Major General Ante Roso are being sent into the field with all their material and technical equipment" isn't it true, sir, that in late 1993 a number of new or additional HV units came into Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't meet with them. I can assure you of that. Towards the end of 1993, I was on sick leave, and I had repeated this on a number of occasions before, and this is the period in which reattachment and restructuring of the units were under preparation by myself and by my deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, witness, for your patience and the Chamber's patience. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's time for a break. Yes, Mr. Krsnik, it's time for a break. We will rise until 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik? Your re-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I'm going to be very brief. Re-examined by Mr. Krsnik:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether you have in front of you the last exhibit, P733. Just one brief question: Can you please tell me, in the Croatian original, are -- at the bottom of the page, there is a function and a signature. Can you tell us whether there is something there before the word "chief"? Yes, see, Witness, I'm talking to you and can you please lower the ELMO, the technical booth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "for the chief."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that somebody else has signed on behalf of the colonel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know that the document speaks for itself but the Prosecutor didn't ask you about this. That's why I wanted to do it. And I again would like to ask you, did the Tuta ATG ever exist as a unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard of such a unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not going to go through all the documents. I have to make sure that my questions are not leading, but I would like to tell you that you have seen a lot of certificates about the affiliation to various units. Your answers are in the transcript. Let me just ask you: Do you know -- did you ever have problems with people who did not want to join the army? Did that problem exist during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The French booth wants to have a break after the question so we can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you please wait for two or three seconds when I stop? Give yourself a break and then start answering. Let me repeat the question: Are you aware of the problem in Herzegovina during the war against the Serbs, as well as during the conflict with Muslims, that there were problems in recruiting people, so to speak? Were there problems with sending troops to the front lines or for the -- with the conscripts being mobilised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I remember, these problems were experienced by Defence offices. They had a problem mobilising new conscripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, if somebody has a certificate that they belong to, for example, the Baja Kraljevic, and they don't belong to that unit, and if that certificate was given to the defence department or defence office, would the defence office then have -- see that as a reason not to mobilise that person to another unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The defence office never checked these certificates, which were produced by the professional units. The defence office would accept such certificate and would not mobilise these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you personally know or do you have any personal examples of ever having caught anybody or anything like that, whether it was widely distributed, whether it existed in big numbers, there were a number of forged certificates to the effect of belonging to any such unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These certificates were used in order for somebody to prove their affiliation to a certain unit, so as to avoid being sent to the front line. There were many such examples, and they -- these were issued by the defence offices and by the units in an equal number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, the operation Cincar that the Prosecutor asked you about, was that a joint operation with the BH Army and the Croatian Army to liberate the western Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That operation was a joint operation, after the Split Agreement, that all the following actions were joint operations, with the participation of the BH Army and the Croatian Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I heard that you were a member of the staff. Can you tell us who was the supreme commander of those operations? Which country was the supreme, whose officers were in command of these operations, the officers of which state?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never met any such high officers. On the axis of the operation of my unit, it was Mr. Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If this is going to be leading, then I will rephrase it. I hope it is not going to be leading. What I wanted to say and ask is whether you are familiar with the fact that the joint operation was commanded by American officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that but I did see them around the headquarters of the Main Staff. I saw them coming there and I -- what I can say is that lower-ranking officers were not informed about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did see American officers in the headquarters of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be so kind to tell us something that I tried to ask every witness? My first question: You personally, under the oath, can you tell the Honourable Chamber whether Mr. Naletilic ever had a rank in the HVO or elsewhere? If the answer is yes, what rank was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, and as far as I'm familiar with the functions exercised by Mr. Naletilic, he was referred to as a general, but he never had a rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order for him to have a rank, would that have to be published in the Official Gazette? The Official Gazette is supposed to carry all the laws and appointments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is yes, this should have been published in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all the ranks published in the Official Gazette?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were published, because there were no ranks until the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the so-called certificates? If yes, can you please tell the Chamber what they are and what they were used for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with certificates. They were distributed in order to entitle somebody to purchase their apartments, shares, and that they were issued based on the time spent in HVO units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you personally know that there were large-scale abuses with these certificates? That's my first question. And second question: The length of the time spent in the army, did it reflect or did it have an impact on the number of certificates issued to that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a large-scale abuse. Certain commanders would issue these certificates even to the people who were not members of their respective units, and I've already said that these certificates were issued to testify the time spent in HVO units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the length of the time spent in the war have an impact on the number and -- or the monetary amount of these certificates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The lists for certificates, are these documents P811, P819, so are these lists for the issuing of certificates? Can you please tell us, these are the lists carrying the name, the Domovina ATJ, where it says that Mr. Martinovic belonged to the Domovina ATJ and to the 22nd detachment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether that was the list for certificates but it may have been because I did not -- I was not familiar with that act and I did not know what its purpose is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par, do you want to re-examine this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions from the judges? Judge Clark, please? Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Witness NR, I have a few questions for you. You described for us a few times that you had been injured and you were "hors de combat" or on furlough and on other occasions that you were on sick leave. Do you make a distinction between being on sick leave and being on furlough because you had been injured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I meant was sick leave. I apologise. I used a wrong word. I was injured four times at the beginning of October, 1993. I was on sick leave, because I had problems with shrapnel that had hit me in the shoulder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you spend any time, for reason of your injury, actually in a hospital bed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In 1994, in early 1994, on the 12th of February, I was severely injured, and I spent the time in hospital. That was until June of the same year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can I take it from that answer that on the previous occasions when you were injured and you were on sick leave, you weren't Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. actually in hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not stay in hospital long, only in October, 1993, when that shrapnel -- I had it removed and I only stayed in hospital for a few days. But since I was in the war all this time, I needed some rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can I ask you, Witness NR, during the period that you were on sick leave, which was fairly extended, I think it was several months, were you at your home in Siroki Brijeg or were you elsewhere in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was in Siroki Brijeg for a short time, and then I was in Croatia where that shrapnel was removed from my shoulder in a hospital in Split.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The main thrust of my question is where did you spend the period of the sick leave after you were discharged from the hospital in Split?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I have relatives in Split, I spent sometime with them, and then I returned to Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I'm going to a different subject now, Witness NR.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Andabak a professional soldier? Did he come from a background of having been a soldier or was he a politician?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was something in between, something between a soldier and a politician. This man was a diabetic and the little time that he spent with the units was really very little. So most of the time he was in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Another witness has given evidence, Mr. NR, and it doesn't necessarily mean that we accept the evidence but we've heard this evidence, that Mr. Andabak really was in charge of -- what's the word in the army, ordering, in charge of logistics and he was in the office most of the time. Would you disagree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was a member of the Convicts Battalion, Mr. Andabak was not engaged in logistics. He was more concerned with the political issues so to speak, and later on, what duties did he discharge, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. After you took up to be safe your other position, shall I say that? When you left the Convicts Battalion, did you have much contact with Mr. Andabak on a -- did you speak to him? Did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did meet. We would have a drink in Siroki Brijeg. Since I was in Mostar most of the time, we did not come across each other that often.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And was it a similar situation with Mr. Naletilic, that it would -- that you would just meet him and have a drink or did you have more contact with Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would meet. We would have a drink but that was all. I didn't have any other contacts with him. We were good friends, and he would inquire about the army, the troops, whether somebody was visiting the families of our fallen soldiers. He was mostly concerned with the troops and we did not have any other deeper, so to say, contacts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: In your unit, which was started later, I have to be very careful because we are in open session, would it be true to say that you and your unit spent little time in Mostar because you were a fire-fighting unit going to various emergency situations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We spent very little time in Mostar. We were sent to the ground, wherever there was an emergency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did you attend the funeral of the late Mr. Mario Hrkac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. He was a very good friend of mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I can imagine if you were sharing or intended to share a flat with him, you must have been good friends. Was he described at the funeral as the commander of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You're quite sure of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander of the Convicts Battalion. What do you mean by "described"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You know when you have a funeral service there is usually somebody who directs an oration or an eulogy and describes the person who has recently died. Was he described as the commander of the Convicts Battalion during the funeral service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The priest who was speaking, I believe that he did mention his name and described him as the commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I've lost your voice, I think. Are you absolutely positive of that, that Mario Hrkac, known as Cikota, was at his funeral described as the commander of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be 100 per cent sure whether he was described in that way, but there were no other eulogies, just the priest who conducted the ceremony said something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And if the funeral were followed in the media, the Croatian newspapers, do you think that Mr. Hrkac would have been described as the fallen commander of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that he would have been. You never know with the media what they are going to say or write.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I couldn't agree more. Thank you very much. You've been very helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of judge's questions? Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one, maybe. Further examination by Mr. Krsnik:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Interpretation] At the funeral was there a lineup of the people and all the other things that would suit a commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, everything was arranged as it would have suited a commander. There were several thousands of people at the funeral. This gentleman had a lot of followers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm sorry I hesitated a moment ago because I didn't know if Judge Diarra would have questions as well, so, yes, Mr. President, a couple of questions following from Judge Clark's questions. Further cross-examination by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll start at the end and work backwards. Concerning any references to Mario Hrkac at the funeral, if you recall, sir, was he described as "a commander" or as "the commander"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the media carried, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm not just talking about the media now and I understand the exchange you and Judge Clark have had about that but you say you were there and apart from what the media said or didn't say, do you remember in this reference to what I'll call a eulogy, assuming that's true, whether the words used were that he was "a" commander of the Convicts Battalion or whether he was described as "the" commander of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the priest mentioned his name and said that the commander of the Convicts Battalion, Mario Hrkac, Cikota, was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.
