In connection with the questions about Mr. Andabak and his military characteristics or activities, on that generally, sir, let me lay the foundations for my questions by asking you this: As a military officer do you believe that it's important to conduct yourself honourably and with integrity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are an officer, that implies you should be honourable and that you should carry out your duty honourably and with integrity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you agree with me, sir, that acting honourably and with integrity includes telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have any of your subordinates ever lied to you, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They may have. I assume they did. Sometimes I knew it, sometimes I didn't. But who can remember everything that happened?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. Let me ask -- let me direct your attention to the times you knew it. You said sometimes you knew it and probably with all the of us sometimes -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this does not arise from Her Honour Judge Clark's questions. This is a new cross-examination, which does not arise from Her Honour Judge Clark's questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I believe that Mr. Scott just laying the ground at this moment. And we are waiting for the question put forward by Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll represent to you very clearly that my question will ultimately tie directly to Mr. Andabak and to the documents before this Court. If I misrepresent that, of course, my questions and the answers can be stricken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The time, sir, that you knew that a subordinate lied to you, what did do you? Did you take any disciplinary action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, please help me. What does that have to do with Judge Clark's questions? We are going to use another hour for the additional cross-examination. Judge Clark was very concrete and she asked the witness what the -- what Mr. Andabak's role was in terms of military duty. Please assist me. I really do not understand. How can the Prosecution have so many more privileges than the Defence? How can they be so much more privileged?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I can't agree with you, Mr. Krsnik. I believe that Mr. Scott promised us that this question will ultimately directly to Mr. Andabak, and the question asked by Judge Clark. You may proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question to you, and I'm trying to ask very few questions, and it's a very simple question, I submitted to you, on an occasion when you knew that one of your subordinate officers had lied to you, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would order disciplinary measures, a few days in prison, or things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you suggesting, sir, that on the probably hundreds of documents that this Chamber may have seen signed by Mr. Andabak, that he was lying when he described Mr. Naletilic as the commander of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say whether Mr. Andabak lied or not. Whatever he did, he should be held accountable for. I cannot comment on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you've told us yourself, sir, repeatedly during your testimony that in your view, Mr. Naletilic was not -- never in 1993 -- excuse me --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, are these questions still questions arising from Judge Clark's questions? And does the question referring to documents signed by Mr. Andabak also arise from Judge Clark's questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I respond very briefly, please, I interpreted, and if I did so wrongly I am sure the Chamber will correct me, I interpreted the questions by Judge Clark to go to Andabak's military involvement, his role in the unit, when he signed, when he was primarily a logistical officer whether he spent most of his time in Siroki Brijeg as opposed to being in the field and all these questions go directly to that and I'm almost finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'll ask Judge Clark to judge it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I was trying to establish the state of Mr. Andabak's knowledge when he wrote those letters. So I'm looking at the content of the letters. So I can see -- I can see how Mr. Scott is interpreted what I was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm trying to conclude, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question, I think the question to you before counsel -- I don't know if we passed it now. What I was beginning to puts to you, sir, was you've told this claim we are that Mr. Naletilic was not the commander of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the Convicts Battalion or the Baja Kraljevic unit during 1993. So I put it to you and I represent to you, and I believe in good faith, just very squarely, if the Chamber has seen numerous documents signed by Mr. Andabak describing Mr. Naletilic as the commander of the Convicts Battalion during 1993, is it your position, are you telling the Chamber, that Mr. Andabak lied? You told us it's important for a military offices to act with integrity. Was he lying?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, allow the witness to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have actually heard ten or 15 questions in your one question. Can you give me one specific question, tell me what you really are interested in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I won't argue with you but I think my question was rather straight forward. Are you telling this Chamber that when Mr. Andabak signed numerous documents describing Mr. Naletilic as the commander of the Convicts Battalion, are you telling the Chamber that he lied when he did so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't say, that he must have lied because Mr. Naletilic was not the commander of the Convicts Battalion in 1993, and as to whether Mr. Andabak should be held accountable for doing that is not up to me to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to help us. When the usher pulls down the blinds, he will show you out of the room. We all wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this has nothing to do with the witness. Just for the record, I would like it to be stated that we spent between nine and 13, under 10 for the cross-examination and that my examination took 29 minutes. I was timing myself. So the cross-examination took five times more than the examination. This is just for the record, and I can only hope that we will be finished by Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have noticed your position and it's registered in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there an documents to tender? Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, Defence would tender document P206.1, if it is not yet been admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry, I don't have the documents in front of me at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I see to save time, on your side, do you have any documents to tender? I understand that some of the documents you used and some are not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: As the Chamber will probably have been able to observe I was skipping and selecting documents as I went, so if the Chamber will allow me I'll make a written submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence number we would give it would be P402 -- I'm sorry, D1/402, formerly P206.1. This was a document that this witness testified concerning last Friday at the very end of his direct examination, and he indicated, after reading this document -- yes, that this document was correct in regards to who was the commander of the Convicts Battalion on December 31, 1992, that being Cikota and other matters that he testified to about concerning this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think we have to look into the record to see whether this document has been admitted into the evidence or not. But if it is admitted we will give it a new number with the D1 document. Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This exhibit was used by Mr. Poriouvaev for the cross-examination and that was the last witness. I don't know whether the Prosecution will ask for the document to be admitted. If they don't we are asking today for this document to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Madam Registrar will check it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it will assist I'm prepared to say if it has not already been admitted, we, the Prosecution does not object to P206.1, which appears to have come from the Zagreb Archive and was indeed marked as a Prosecution exhibit so we are not -- we wouldn't be in a position to dispute that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So this document is admitted into the evidence since both parties agreed on this point. And could we have the next witness? Are there any protective measures for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, just as was the case so far. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I guess there is no objections from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your request is granted. Mr. Usher could we have the next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Mr. Krsnik, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Krsnik:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, witness, could you please approach closer to the microphones? No, no, do not take off your jacket, please. I apologise, if you would feel more comfortable without the jacket, I guess you can take it off. On this piece of paper, you will see your name written. Please do not pronounce it. Just say yes if this is your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very brief instructions. Whenever I put a question to you, could you please wait for three seconds and start with your answer? Can you do it please? Because this is how you're going to help us all. Once you have noticed my question having been completed, please count to three and then start answering your question. Is that fine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have to facilitate the work of our interpreters, and this is important for everybody's sake. Could you please, very briefly introduce yourself to this Chamber without mentioning your name, when you were born, when you finished your schools, where you're living and where you work.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: I was born on the 13th of August in 1959 in Mostar. I completed elementary and secondary schools in Mostar. I graduated from a faculty in Zagreb. I have now been living and working in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'll be putting to you very specific questions about specific years. Everything that I'm going to ask you about will be put into the following time horizon. From April 1993 to the end of 1993. This is the periods to which my questions will be related. Tell us, in this period, were you a member of HVO, and if you were, of which unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: The commander of this brigade was Ilija Vrljic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look towards me? We will have to slow down a little because it seems to me that we are having a great deal of problems and you're also requested to slow down. Please wait for three seconds and slow down. How many battalions did this brigade consist of?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps this would be a good point to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So from the north, the BH Army brigades attacked Bijelo Polje together with Zuka's people and some other people, I don't know who. Some of the mujahedin, containing aggression troops and units. From the south, we were also attacked, from Mostar, from -- where their sabotage platoons and their army that was available to them attacked us. Inside Bijelo Polje itself, people of Muslim ethnicity, members of the HVO, together with other Muslim population living in Bijelo Polje, attacked us on that morning, morning of that day, they captured and killed some of our people. Each HVO soldier was rounded during that night. Some managed to escape. However, most were captured and killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: The civilians were also captured. There were children and women there who, during the attack, were also raped. Many of them were killed. During those parties and celebrations that they organised in the outpatient clinic where the medical staff, the doctors, were half of Muslim, half of Croatian origin, and they turned their weapons against the friends who they used to party with. Some were killed and others were captured in a cruel manner. This went on in other areas as well, where my Sabotage Unit members were killed, those who wanted to go to join the parties. I too was invited to a birthday party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. You did not answer her Honour's Judge Diarra's questions. Where were they taken and where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: The HVO members of Croat ethnicity that were captured by the BH army were take to the camps in Bijelo Polje, the school building in Bijelo Polje, and from there, they were then transferred further. Some soldiers were directly transferred to Mostar, to the 4th elementary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: The civilian population as far as I know were taken to the school. Inside the school there was this camp for the civilian population, for women and children. While the soldiers were transferred to Mostar, while they were maltreated and tortured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally witness that the population of Bijelo Polje of Croat origin had to dig the trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: Yes. We were on the other side of the Neretva River and we were able to see those -- them, the civilian population, digging our trenches. We were defending ourselves there and on the opposite side of the front line there was the BH Army, who deployed our own people who were not far away and we were able to observe them, who, throughout the day, were mercilessly forced to labour, and we also witnessed the torture that they were exposed to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I don't think there is any dispute on this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll proceed. I just wanted to focus on June the 30th, because it is included both in the indictment and the witness, this gentleman, was brought here for a very specific reason, which is familiar to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your battalion, did you have -- well, how to call them -- members of a sabotage group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: Yes in my battalion I had a Sabotage Unit known as Ivan Stanisic, and it was named after our member who had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we go into private session, please? I apologise, Your Honours, for asking you to do that on and off?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to describe the Chamber how you know him, how well you know him, and when you met him for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: I've known him as a person who participated in the liberation of Mostar, liberation from the Serb aggressors, and I know him as a legend of this war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he ever your commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: No. He was never my commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the 1993 and the period from April to the end of 1993, did you ever, together with Mr. Naletilic, attend any meeting whatsoever? And I'm particularly referring to the headquarters and to the chief in command in your camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: No. I never attended a meeting of this sort which would be held in the brigade headquarters in the northern operative zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a person known as Miro Kolobara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the name of Kolobara is quite a common name in Bijelo Polje, and I think I know two or three persons with this name. I don't know who you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Neither do I. I just want to know whether you are familiar with the fact that any of these persons under this name would be members of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: No. If this were the case, I would certainly be familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the three Kolobara persons, which units members they were, if they were members of any units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: Miro Kolobara, the first, was a member of my battalion during the war against the Serbs. He was captured then, and he was taken to the Trebinje camp. Later, he was exchanged for other prisoners of war, and he then joined another battalion, because Vrapcici is an area which was covered by another battalion. Furthermore, I'm familiar with another person by the name of Miro Kolobara. He came from Livce. That's a part of Bijelo Polje. During the attack of the Serbs, his parents were killed. At that time, he was also injured. He escaped, and I never saw him again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My two final questions: Do you know that in the autumn of 1993, in Siroki Brijeg, there would be some BH Army members detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: Since I was in contact with Berko Pusic, who was in charge of the prisoners exchange office, I asked him to do his best to include members of my battalion who were captured in the exchange operations, in the prisoner exchange operations. He told me that they had some two BH Army members who had been captured. They had them in Siroki Brijeg. That the other party has shown very keen interest in them. I went to Siroki Brijeg myself to see these two persons. He told me that they were stationed in the military police building so I went there. I went there, I introduced myself, and they allowed me to visit these two captured members of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them? Were they from Bijelo Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They were from Bijelo Polje, i.e. from Vrapcici more specifically and they had previously been my soldiers. One of them recognised me. We would greet each other. He smiled at me and he seemed to be very happy to see me. And then we talked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw them, did you also see some other individuals detained, members of the HVO or others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: Yes. It seemed to me that other two members of the HVO were detained because I heard them talking, in addition to these two BH Army members, none of them were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go back to Bijelo Polje? Did you inform Mr. Bisha? Did the exchange of the prisoners take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: Yes. I promised these two persons that we'll do our best to include them in the prisoners' exchange activities because a lot of my people were detained. I also came back to Mostar then. I informed Berko Pusic about what I had seen, and I asked him to do his best for the prisoner exchange to take place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the prisoner exchange take place? And if it did, when? This is my last question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: The exchange, I think, took place much later. I couldn't go to Mostar because the BH Army repeatedly attacked the town during day and during night hours, to expel us, to get us away from the right bank, and I was no longer in contact with Berko -- well, in fact I was in contact with him but not in relation to these two soldiers, and the exchange took place later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was just reminded that I need to put another question to you: Do you know the names, first or family name, of these individuals, how they looked like, and when you saw them, did you notice on them any traces of torture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: Their names were Maric. I don't know his first name. They seemed in a good shape, according to my understanding, given the time and the circumstances. They looked exhausted. They were very thin but so were all of us who were involved in this war. I noticed no signs of torture or maltreat on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe them, how tall were they, what was the colour of their hair, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: Well that was a long time ago. I can only recall that one of them was fairly tall, and the other one was fairly short.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My final question, and I see that we are approaching the end of today's time, and this will be my -- the end of my examination-in-chief: Did Brko tell us why the army was so -- the BH Army was -- had shown such keen interest in their being included in the prisoner exchange?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: Yes, he told me that he had or they had in fact a relative who was a commander in the BH Army, and that these two individuals were very significant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a commander by the name of Maric in Bijelo Polje? Do you have any personal knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. This is all, Your Honours. I don't think there can be any doubt how long my examination-in-chief took. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, I'm afraid that we have to keep you in The Hague for another day. So I have to remind you, as I did to other witnesses, that during your stay in The Hague, do not talk to anybody about your testimony and do not let anybody talk to you about it. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 1.45 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 2nd day of June, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25
